title: Strength Meaning: Put Your Energy into Staying Steady

quickTake.upright: Keep your composure and act with courage. A gentle approach can still get things done.
quickTake.reversed: Pushing harder is making things worse. Are you forcing yourself to keep going, or trying to overpower someone else?

hook: Strength can have a light touch. Under pressure, this card asks how you use the energy you have.

sections.title: Look at her hands, then the lion’s body
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Against a broad yellow background, a woman in white bends toward an orange-red lion. She wears a flower crown, and a garland at her waist hangs beside its mane. A sideways figure eight floats above her head. One hand rests near its upper jaw; the other supports the lower jaw. Neither arm is raised to strike. The lion lifts its head with its mouth open and tongue showing. Its tail curls between its hind legs, and all four paws remain on the ground.

She wears no armour, and there are no weapons in the scene. Her dress falls vertically while the lion’s body stretches sideways. Their contrasting postures meet at her hands. Behind them lie green ground, trees and a blue mountain, with plenty of open space. Notice these visible relationships before naming the action: a still image alone cannot establish whether she is opening or closing the lion’s mouth. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_08_Strength.jpg)

sections.title: Waite’s Strength has a religious context
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Waite explicitly describes her as closing the lion’s jaws. He says her beneficent fortitude has already subdued it, and associates the flower chain with divine law. In one of his interpretations, the lion represents the passions. He also distinguishes religious trust from ordinary self-confidence. Reducing his account to “believe in yourself and you will succeed” leaves out that context. [Waite, Part II, VIII](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar08.htm)

The discussion of feelings and action below is DestinyPixel’s reflective reading for present-day life. The figures’ genders do not prescribe who must be gentle or who needs to be tamed.

sections.title: Upright: Give courage a practical form
sections.bodyMarkdown:
An upright reading can suggest staying clear-headed and continuing with what needs doing, even when it is difficult. Anger may alert you to a boundary being crossed; fear may show that something matters. Recognise the feeling first, then choose a response. That gives your strength a direction.

Gentleness can be firm. Clearly saying “I cannot meet that request” differs from repeatedly giving way. If you are already exhausted, asking for support or reducing the task can also protect your ability to act.

sections.title: Reversed: Notice both kinds of imbalance
sections.bodyMarkdown: Start with two possibilities. You may be trying to control everything through pressure, blame or a show of toughness. Or prolonged strain may have left you without the energy even to express a need. Waite’s old list includes both abuse of power and weakness. Our further suggestion is to examine triggers and workload before labelling yourself “not strong enough.” [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 8](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

sections.title: When you want to push back, or just keep going
sections.bodyMarkdown:
A client adds a last-minute request. An upright Strength exercise would be to listen, then set out the additional scope, a realistic delivery date and what else must change. Reversed, check whether your tone is becoming harsher, or whether you keep saying yes to work you cannot finish.

When learning a skill, repeated failures can tempt you to practise for much longer. Try correcting one movement and making room for rest. During an argument, returning after a ten-minute pause may help more than raising your voice. If there are threats or harm, your safety and access to support come first. This card does not ask you to change someone through patience.

sections.title: Practice: Give your energy somewhere to go
sections.bodyMarkdown: Recall a recent moment when you nearly lost control. Write three lines: what I felt; what I wanted to protect; what I could say next time to express a boundary. Practise one actual sentence, such as “I am willing to deal with this, but I need until tomorrow to reply.”

sections.title: A common misreading
sections.bodyMarkdown: Strength does not mean never feeling angry, or becoming more virtuous the longer you endure. The contact in the picture can help you think about regulation and courage. It cannot establish who is inherently strong or weak, or decide how much you should tolerate.

articleMarkdown:
# Strength Meaning: Put Your Energy into Staying Steady

Card: Strength  
Number: VIII · RWS Major Arcana  
Keywords: Courage, Patience, Self-regulation

**Upright quick take:** Keep your composure and act with courage. A gentle approach can still get things done.  
**Reversed quick take:** Pushing harder is making things worse. Are you forcing yourself to keep going, or trying to overpower someone else?

Strength can have a light touch. Under pressure, this card asks how you use the energy you have.

## Look at her hands, then the lion’s body

Against a broad yellow background, a woman in white bends toward an orange-red lion. She wears a flower crown, and a garland at her waist hangs beside its mane. A sideways figure eight floats above her head. One hand rests near its upper jaw; the other supports the lower jaw. Neither arm is raised to strike. The lion lifts its head with its mouth open and tongue showing. Its tail curls between its hind legs, and all four paws remain on the ground.

She wears no armour, and there are no weapons in the scene. Her dress falls vertically while the lion’s body stretches sideways. Their contrasting postures meet at her hands. Behind them lie green ground, trees and a blue mountain, with plenty of open space. Notice these visible relationships before naming the action: a still image alone cannot establish whether she is opening or closing the lion’s mouth. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_08_Strength.jpg)

## Waite’s Strength has a religious context

Waite explicitly describes her as closing the lion’s jaws. He says her beneficent fortitude has already subdued it, and associates the flower chain with divine law. In one of his interpretations, the lion represents the passions. He also distinguishes religious trust from ordinary self-confidence. Reducing his account to “believe in yourself and you will succeed” leaves out that context. [Waite, Part II, VIII](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar08.htm)

The discussion of feelings and action below is DestinyPixel’s reflective reading for present-day life. The figures’ genders do not prescribe who must be gentle or who needs to be tamed.

## Upright: Give courage a practical form

An upright reading can suggest staying clear-headed and continuing with what needs doing, even when it is difficult. Anger may alert you to a boundary being crossed; fear may show that something matters. Recognise the feeling first, then choose a response. That gives your strength a direction.

Gentleness can be firm. Clearly saying “I cannot meet that request” differs from repeatedly giving way. If you are already exhausted, asking for support or reducing the task can also protect your ability to act.

## Reversed: Notice both kinds of imbalance

Start with two possibilities. You may be trying to control everything through pressure, blame or a show of toughness. Or prolonged strain may have left you without the energy even to express a need. Waite’s old list includes both abuse of power and weakness. Our further suggestion is to examine triggers and workload before labelling yourself “not strong enough.” [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 8](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

## When you want to push back, or just keep going

A client adds a last-minute request. An upright Strength exercise would be to listen, then set out the additional scope, a realistic delivery date and what else must change. Reversed, check whether your tone is becoming harsher, or whether you keep saying yes to work you cannot finish.

When learning a skill, repeated failures can tempt you to practise for much longer. Try correcting one movement and making room for rest. During an argument, returning after a ten-minute pause may help more than raising your voice. If there are threats or harm, your safety and access to support come first. This card does not ask you to change someone through patience.

## Practice: Give your energy somewhere to go

Recall a recent moment when you nearly lost control. Write three lines: what I felt; what I wanted to protect; what I could say next time to express a boundary. Practise one actual sentence, such as “I am willing to deal with this, but I need until tomorrow to reply.”

## A common misreading

Strength does not mean never feeling angry, or becoming more virtuous the longer you endure. The contact in the picture can help you think about regulation and courage. It cannot establish who is inherently strong or weak, or decide how much you should tolerate.

## Read next

The Chariot: compare outward momentum with steadiness in your own responses; Temperance: explore how to adjust effort and pace.

sourceRecord.hook: 有力量的人，也能把动作放轻。遇到压力时，这张牌关心你怎样使用那股劲。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 稳得住脾气，也拿得出勇气，柔和一点照样能把事做好。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 越使劲越拧巴，看看自己是在硬撑，还是想把别人压住。

sections.title: 先看她的手，再看狮子的身体
paragraphs: 大片黄色背景里，一位白衣女子俯身面对橙红色狮子。她头戴花冠，腰间的花串垂到狮鬃旁；头顶悬着横向的「8」形符号。一只手靠在狮子的上颚，另一只托着下颚，手臂没有挥打的姿态。狮子抬头张嘴，露出舌头，尾巴卷到两条后腿之间，四爪仍落在地面。
她没有盔甲，画面也没有武器。衣服向下垂落，狮子的身体横向展开，一静一动在双手接触处相遇。后方是绿地、树丛和一座蓝色山峰，视野相当开阔。先记住这些可见的关系，再给动作命名；静止图像本身并不能证明她是在掰开还是合拢狮口。[查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_08_Strength.jpg)

sections.title: Waite 说的力量有宗教背景
paragraphs: Waite 明确把动作写成「合上狮子的嘴」，并解释狮子已被温厚的坚毅制伏，花链则承载神圣律法的象征。他把狮子的一层含义联系到激情，也特意区分自己的宗教性信赖与日常自信。因此，把这张牌直接概括成「相信自己就会成功」，会漏掉原文的语境。[Waite 第二部 VIII](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar08.htm)
下面用它讨论情绪与行动，是本站面向今天生活的反思式读法；这也不是把人物的性别变成谁必须温柔、谁需要被驯服的规定。

sections.title: 正位 把勇气放进具体动作
paragraphs: 正位可读作：事情有难度，你仍能保持清醒，持续做该做的事。愤怒提醒你有边界被碰到，害怕说明这件事重要；先识别感受，再决定怎样回应，力量就有了方向。
温和也可以很坚决。清楚说「这个要求我做不到」，与反复忍让是两回事。若已经疲惫，寻求支援、缩小任务，同样能让你保住行动能力。

sections.title: 逆位 留意失衡的两头
paragraphs: 逆位可从两处查起：一头是总想控制局面，用催促、责备或逞强维持秩序；另一头是长期消耗后，连表达需要的力气也没了。Waite 的旧词表同时包含滥用力量与软弱，已提示这两种可能。本站进一步建议先找触发点和负荷，而不是给自己贴「不够强」的标签。[Waite 第三部 §3，第8条](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

sections.title: 当你想顶回去，或只想撑下去
paragraphs: 工作中，客户临时加需求。力量正位的练习可以是先听完，再列出新增范围、可交付日期与需要调整的部分；逆位则提醒你留意，是语气越来越冲，还是明明做不完仍一口答应。
练习一项技能时，连续失败容易让人猛加时长。可改为只修正一个动作，并给休息留位置。关系争执里，暂停十分钟后再谈，比继续提高音量更可能让问题说清；若存在威胁或伤害，保护自己和获得帮助优先，牌意不要求你靠耐心改变对方。

sections.title: 练习 让力气有一个落点
paragraphs: 写下最近一次差点失控的时刻，分成三行：我当时有什么感受；我想保护什么；下次可以用哪句具体的话表达边界。选一句实际练习，例如「我愿意处理这件事，但需要明天再给答复」。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 力量不等于永不生气，也不等于忍耐越久越高尚。图中的接触可以帮助你思考调节与勇气，却不能证明任何人天生强弱，或替你决定该忍受多少。
